question: A point $P(x,y)$ moves in the first quadrant along the circle $x^2+y^2=100$. Its $x$-coordinate increases at a constant rate of $3\ \text{units/s}$. When $P=(6,8)$, determine the instantaneous velocity and acceleration of its $y$-coordinate, and hence obtain the equations of the tangent and normal to the circle at $P$, explaining how the derivative represents the tangent slope.
explanation:
Rate Relation
Differentiating $x^2+y^2=100$ with respect to time,
$$2x\frac{dx}{dt}+2y\frac{dy}{dt}=0$$
Therefore,
$$\frac{dy}{dt}=-\frac{x}{y}\frac{dx}{dt}$$
At $(6,8)$, with $\frac{dx}{dt}=3$,
$$\frac{dy}{dt}=-\frac{6}{8}(3)=-\frac{9}{4}\ \text{units/s}$$
Thus, the $y$-coordinate is decreasing at $\frac{9}{4}\ \text{units/s}$.

Acceleration
Differentiating $x\frac{dx}{dt}+y\frac{dy}{dt}=0$ again,
$$\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)^2+x\frac{d^2x}{dt^2}+\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)^2+y\frac{d^2y}{dt^2}=0$$
Since the $x$-coordinate increases at a constant rate, $\frac{d^2x}{dt^2}=0$. Hence,
$$9+\frac{81}{16}+8\frac{d^2y}{dt^2}=0$$
$$8\frac{d^2y}{dt^2}=-\frac{225}{16}$$
$$\frac{d^2y}{dt^2}=-\frac{225}{128}\ \text{units/s}^2$$

Tangent and Normal
Differentiating the circle with respect to $x$,
$$2x+2y\frac{dy}{dx}=0$$
$$\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{x}{y}$$
At $(6,8)$, the tangent slope is $-\frac{3}{4}$. This derivative gives the instantaneous direction of the curve at $P$. The tangent is
$$y-8=-\frac{3}{4}(x-6)$$
or
$$3x+4y=50$$
The normal slope is $\frac{4}{3}$, so the normal is
$$y-8=\frac{4}{3}(x-6)$$

options.D: $\frac{dy}{dt}=-\frac{9}{4}$ units/s, $\frac{d^2y}{dt^2}=-\frac{225}{128}$ units/s$^2$; tangent $3x+4y=50$; normal $y-8=\frac{4}{3}(x-6)$; $\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{3}{4}$ is the tangent slope
